title: Flag Low Stock SKUs Below Reorder Trigger
description_markdown: Supply chain alert: Find all items in `stock_items` where `quantity_on_hand <= reorder_level`. Return `sku`, `name`, `quantity_on_hand`, and `reorder_level`. Order by `quantity_on_hand` ASC, `sku` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Stock below reorder point
SELECT sku, name, quantity_on_hand, reorder_level FROM stock_items WHERE ...
solution_query: SELECT sku, name, quantity_on_hand, reorder_level FROM stock_items WHERE quantity_on_hand <= reorder_level ORDER BY quantity_on_hand ASC, sku ASC;
solution_explanation: Generates replenishment purchase orders for low-stock SKUs.
hints: Use `WHERE quantity_on_hand <= reorder_level`.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.
Query: SELECT sku, name, quantity_on_hand, reorder_level FROM stock_items WHERE quantity_on_hand <= reorder_level ORDER BY quantity_on_hand ASC, sku ASC;

title: Compute Total Inventory Valuation per Warehouse
description_markdown: Finance request: For each warehouse in `warehouses`, calculate the total inventory valuation (`SUM(quantity_on_hand * unit_cost)` as `total_valuation`). Return `w.name AS warehouse_name`, `w.location`, and `total_valuation`. Order by `total_valuation` DESC.
starter_query:
-- Warehouse inventory valuation
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT w.name AS warehouse_name, w.location, SUM(s.quantity_on_hand * s.unit_cost) AS total_valuation FROM warehouses w JOIN stock_items s ON w.warehouse_id = s.warehouse_id GROUP BY w.warehouse_id, w.name, w.location ORDER BY total_valuation DESC, w.warehouse_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Multiplies on-hand units by acquisition unit costs and aggregates across facilities.
hints: Multiply `s.quantity_on_hand * s.unit_cost` inside SUM.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.

Query: SELECT w.name AS warehouse_name, w.location, SUM(s.quantity_on_hand * s.unit_cost) AS total_valuation FROM warehouses w JOIN stock_items s ON w.warehouse_id = s.warehouse_id GROUP BY w.warehouse_id, w.name, w.location ORDER BY total_valuation DESC, w.warehouse_id ASC;

title: Supplier Lead Volume and Country Concentration
description_markdown: Procurement request: Group by supplier (`suppliers`) to calculate count of unique SKUs provided (`COUNT(s.item_id)` as `supplied_skus`), and total stock held across facilities (`SUM(s.quantity_on_hand)` as `total_units`). Return `sp.name AS supplier_name`, `sp.country`, `supplied_skus`, and `total_units`. Order by `total_units` DESC, `sp.supplier_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Supplier metrics
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT sp.name AS supplier_name, sp.country, COUNT(s.item_id) AS supplied_skus, SUM(s.quantity_on_hand) AS total_units FROM suppliers sp JOIN stock_items s ON sp.supplier_id = s.supplier_id GROUP BY sp.supplier_id, sp.name, sp.country ORDER BY total_units DESC, sp.supplier_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Audits supplier exposure and inventory concentration risks.
hints: Join suppliers with stock_items.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.

Query: SELECT sp.name AS supplier_name, sp.country, COUNT(s.item_id) AS supplied_skus, SUM(s.quantity_on_hand) AS total_units FROM suppliers sp JOIN stock_items s ON sp.supplier_id = s.supplier_id GROUP BY sp.supplier_id, sp.name, sp.country ORDER BY total_units DESC, sp.supplier_id ASC;

description_markdown: Retrieve all regional logistics hubs from `warehouses` with a storage capacity of at least 40,000 units (`capacity >= 40000`). Return `warehouse_id`, `name`, `location`, and `capacity`. Order by `capacity` DESC, `warehouse_id` ASC.

Order by `capacity` DESC, `warehouse_id` ASC.

Query: SELECT sku, name, unit_cost FROM stock_items WHERE unit_cost > 20.00 ORDER BY unit_cost DESC, sku ASC;

title: List International Component Suppliers Outside USA
description_markdown: Procurement compliance check: Retrieve all vendors from `suppliers` whose headquarters are outside the United States (`country != 'USA'`). Return `supplier_id`, `name`, `country`, and `contact_email`. Order by `country` ASC, `name` ASC.

Order by `country` ASC, `name` ASC.

title: Aggregate Company-Wide Inventory Volume and Unit Cost
description_markdown: Compute aggregate totals across all items in `stock_items`: total on-hand quantity (`SUM(quantity_on_hand)` as `total_units`) and average unit acquisition cost (`ROUND(AVG(unit_cost), 2)` as `avg_unit_cost`).
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT SUM(quantity_on_hand) AS total_units, ROUND(AVG(unit_cost), 2) AS avg_unit_cost FROM stock_items;
solution_explanation: Aggregates overall unit volume and mean cost baseline.
hints: Use `SUM(quantity_on_hand)` and `ROUND(AVG(unit_cost), 2)`.
No GROUP BY clause is necessary for full-table aggregation.
Query: SELECT SUM(quantity_on_hand) AS total_units, ROUND(AVG(unit_cost), 2) AS avg_unit_cost FROM stock_items;

title: Classify Inventory Health and Stocking Thresholds
description_markdown:
Supply chain dashboard: Categorize items in `stock_items` using a `CASE` expression as `stock_status`:
- If `quantity_on_hand <= 10`, return `'Critical'`
- Else if `quantity_on_hand <= reorder_level`, return `'Low'`
- Otherwise, return `'Adequate'`

Return `sku`, `name`, `quantity_on_hand`, `reorder_level`, and `stock_status`. Order by `quantity_on_hand` ASC, `sku` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT sku, name, quantity_on_hand, reorder_level, CASE WHEN quantity_on_hand <= 10 THEN 'Critical' WHEN quantity_on_hand <= reorder_level THEN 'Low' ELSE 'Adequate' END AS stock_status FROM stock_items ORDER BY quantity_on_hand ASC, sku ASC;
solution_explanation: Applies conditional evaluation to inventory levels.
hints: Use `CASE WHEN quantity_on_hand <= 10 THEN 'Critical' WHEN quantity_on_hand <= reorder_level THEN 'Low' ELSE 'Adequate' END`.
Order by `quantity_on_hand` ASC, `sku` ASC.

Query: SELECT sku, name, quantity_on_hand, reorder_level, CASE WHEN quantity_on_hand <= 10 THEN 'Critical' WHEN quantity_on_hand <= reorder_level THEN 'Low' ELSE 'Adequate' END AS stock_status FROM stock_items ORDER BY quantity_on_hand ASC, sku ASC;

title: Summarize Inventory Transactions by Movement Type
description_markdown: Logistics audit: For each `transaction_type` in `stock_transactions`, count total transactions (`COUNT(tx_id)` as `tx_count`) and aggregate moved units (`SUM(quantity)` as `total_qty`). Return `transaction_type`, `tx_count`, and `total_qty`. Order by `tx_count` DESC, `transaction_type` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT transaction_type, COUNT(tx_id) AS tx_count, SUM(quantity) AS total_qty FROM stock_transactions GROUP BY transaction_type ORDER BY tx_count DESC, transaction_type ASC;
solution_explanation: Groups warehouse inventory operations by transaction type.
hints: Group by `transaction_type`.
Aggregate with `COUNT(tx_id)` and `SUM(quantity)`.
Query: SELECT transaction_type, COUNT(tx_id) AS tx_count, SUM(quantity) AS total_qty FROM stock_transactions GROUP BY transaction_type ORDER BY tx_count DESC, transaction_type ASC;

title: Count Distinct SKUs Stored per Warehouse Facility
description_markdown: Count how many distinct catalog SKUs are stored at each facility. Join `warehouses` with `stock_items`. Return `w.warehouse_id`, `w.name`, and `COUNT(s.item_id)` as `sku_count`. Order by `sku_count` DESC, `w.warehouse_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT w.warehouse_id, w.name, COUNT(s.item_id) AS sku_count FROM warehouses w JOIN stock_items s ON w.warehouse_id = s.warehouse_id GROUP BY w.warehouse_id, w.name ORDER BY sku_count DESC, w.warehouse_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Inner joins warehouses with catalog items and counts records per facility.
hints: Join `warehouses w` and `stock_items s` on `w.warehouse_id = s.warehouse_id`.
Group by `w.warehouse_id, w.name` and order by `sku_count` DESC, `w.warehouse_id` ASC.

Query: SELECT w.warehouse_id, w.name, COUNT(s.item_id) AS sku_count FROM warehouses w JOIN stock_items s ON w.warehouse_id = s.warehouse_id GROUP BY w.warehouse_id, w.name ORDER BY sku_count DESC, w.warehouse_id ASC;

title: Map Catalog Items to Sourcing Vendors and Origin Countries
description_markdown: Produce a sourcing lookup mapping each item in `stock_items` to its vendor in `suppliers`. Return `s.sku`, `s.name AS item_name`, `sp.name AS supplier_name`, and `sp.country`. Order by `s.sku` ASC.
starter_query:

SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT s.sku, s.name AS item_name, sp.name AS supplier_name, sp.country FROM stock_items s JOIN suppliers sp ON s.supplier_id = sp.supplier_id ORDER BY s.sku ASC;
solution_explanation: Joins inventory items to primary suppliers.
hints: Join `stock_items s` and `suppliers sp` on `s.supplier_id = sp.supplier_id`.
Alias columns as `item_name` and `supplier_name`.
Query: SELECT s.sku, s.name AS item_name, sp.name AS supplier_name, sp.country FROM stock_items s JOIN suppliers sp ON s.supplier_id = sp.supplier_id ORDER BY s.sku ASC;

title: Audit Inbound Restocking Purchase Transactions
description_markdown: Filter all inbound inventory movements (`transaction_type = 'inbound'`). Join `stock_transactions` with `stock_items`. Return `t.tx_id`, `s.sku`, `s.name`, `t.quantity`, and `t.tx_date`. Order by `t.tx_date` ASC, `t.tx_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT t.tx_id, s.sku, s.name, t.quantity, t.tx_date FROM stock_transactions t JOIN stock_items s ON t.item_id = s.item_id WHERE t.transaction_type = 'inbound' ORDER BY t.tx_date ASC, t.tx_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Audits inbound fulfillment intake events.
hints: Join on `t.item_id = s.item_id` with `WHERE t.transaction_type = 'inbound'`.
Order by `t.tx_date` ASC, `t.tx_id` ASC.

Query: SELECT t.tx_id, s.sku, s.name, t.quantity, t.tx_date FROM stock_transactions t JOIN stock_items s ON t.item_id = s.item_id WHERE t.transaction_type = 'inbound' ORDER BY t.tx_date ASC, t.tx_id ASC;

title: Calculate Line-Item Inventory Valuation
description_markdown: Financial accounting: For each product in `stock_items`, calculate the total inventory valuation (`quantity_on_hand * unit_cost` as `inventory_value`). Return `sku`, `name`, `quantity_on_hand`, `unit_cost`, and `inventory_value`. Order by `inventory_value` DESC, `sku` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT sku, name, quantity_on_hand, unit_cost, (quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) AS inventory_value FROM stock_items ORDER BY inventory_value DESC, sku ASC;
solution_explanation: Multiplies current on-hand units by acquisition unit price.
hints: Multiply `quantity_on_hand * unit_cost` as `inventory_value`.
Order by `inventory_value` DESC, `sku` ASC.
Query: SELECT sku, name, quantity_on_hand, unit_cost, (quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) AS inventory_value FROM stock_items ORDER BY inventory_value DESC, sku ASC;

title: Identify Hubs Operating Above Average Facility Capacity
description_markdown: Facilities strategy: Identify warehouses whose storage capacity is strictly greater than the average capacity across all warehouses. Return `warehouse_id`, `name`, and `capacity`. Order by `capacity` DESC, `warehouse_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT warehouse_id, name, capacity FROM warehouses WHERE capacity > (SELECT AVG(capacity) FROM warehouses) ORDER BY capacity DESC, warehouse_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Applies a scalar subquery in the WHERE clause.
hints: Use `WHERE capacity > (SELECT AVG(capacity) FROM warehouses)`.
Order by `capacity` DESC, `warehouse_id` ASC.
Query: SELECT warehouse_id, name, capacity FROM warehouses WHERE capacity > (SELECT AVG(capacity) FROM warehouses) ORDER BY capacity DESC, warehouse_id ASC;

title: Filter High-Breadth Suppliers Providing Multiple SKUs
description_markdown: Find suppliers in `suppliers` that manufacture or supply more than one distinct item (`COUNT(s.item_id) > 1`). Return `sp.supplier_id`, `sp.name`, and `COUNT(s.item_id)` as `item_count`. Order by `item_count` DESC, `sp.supplier_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT sp.supplier_id, sp.name, COUNT(s.item_id) AS item_count FROM suppliers sp JOIN stock_items s ON sp.supplier_id = s.supplier_id GROUP BY sp.supplier_id, sp.name HAVING COUNT(s.item_id) > 1 ORDER BY item_count DESC, sp.supplier_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Uses HAVING to filter grouped vendor catalogs.
hints: Join `suppliers sp` and `stock_items s` on `sp.supplier_id = s.supplier_id`.
Group by `sp.supplier_id, sp.name` and filter with `HAVING COUNT(s.item_id) > 1`.

Query: SELECT sp.supplier_id, sp.name, COUNT(s.item_id) AS item_count FROM suppliers sp JOIN stock_items s ON sp.supplier_id = s.supplier_id GROUP BY sp.supplier_id, sp.name HAVING COUNT(s.item_id) > 1 ORDER BY item_count DESC, sp.supplier_id ASC;

title: Compute Net Transaction Flow per Catalog Item
description_markdown: Calculate net unit movement for items that have transactions: inbound receipts increase stock (`+quantity`), outbound shipments decrease stock (`-quantity`). Group by item. Return `s.item_id`, `s.sku`, `s.name`, and the net total as `net_movement`. Order by `net_movement` DESC, `s.item_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT s.item_id, s.sku, s.name, SUM(CASE WHEN t.transaction_type = 'inbound' THEN t.quantity WHEN t.transaction_type = 'outbound' THEN -t.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS net_movement FROM stock_items s JOIN stock_transactions t ON s.item_id = t.item_id GROUP BY s.item_id, s.sku, s.name ORDER BY net_movement DESC, s.item_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Uses conditional aggregation across transaction types.
hints: Use `SUM(CASE WHEN t.transaction_type = 'inbound' THEN t.quantity WHEN t.transaction_type = 'outbound' THEN -t.quantity ELSE 0 END)`.
Group by `s.item_id, s.sku, s.name` and order by `net_movement` DESC, `s.item_id` ASC.

Query: SELECT s.item_id, s.sku, s.name, SUM(CASE WHEN t.transaction_type = 'inbound' THEN t.quantity WHEN t.transaction_type = 'outbound' THEN -t.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS net_movement FROM stock_items s JOIN stock_transactions t ON s.item_id = t.item_id GROUP BY s.item_id, s.sku, s.name ORDER BY net_movement DESC, s.item_id ASC;

title: Identify Dormant SKUs with Zero Transaction History
description_markdown: Audit dormant stock: Find all items in `stock_items` that have never had any recorded transactions in `stock_transactions`. Return `s.item_id`, `s.sku`, `s.name`, and `s.quantity_on_hand`. Order by `s.item_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT s.item_id, s.sku, s.name, s.quantity_on_hand FROM stock_items s LEFT JOIN stock_transactions t ON s.item_id = t.item_id WHERE t.tx_id IS NULL ORDER BY s.item_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Anti-join using LEFT JOIN and IS NULL filter.
hints: Left join `stock_items s` with `stock_transactions t` on `s.item_id = t.item_id`.
Filter with `WHERE t.tx_id IS NULL`.
Query: SELECT s.item_id, s.sku, s.name, s.quantity_on_hand FROM stock_items s LEFT JOIN stock_transactions t ON s.item_id = t.item_id WHERE t.tx_id IS NULL ORDER BY s.item_id ASC;

title: Calculate Warehouse Capacity Utilization Percentages
description_markdown: Calculate capacity utilization for each facility: sum current on-hand units (`COALESCE(SUM(s.quantity_on_hand), 0)` as `total_units_stored`) and compute the percentage of storage capacity filled: `ROUND((COALESCE(SUM(s.quantity_on_hand), 0) * 100.0) / w.capacity, 2)` as `utilization_pct`. Return `w.warehouse_id`, `w.name`, `w.capacity`, `total_units_stored`, and `utilization_pct`. Order by `utilization_pct` DESC, `w.warehouse_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT w.warehouse_id, w.name, w.capacity, COALESCE(SUM(s.quantity_on_hand), 0) AS total_units_stored, ROUND((COALESCE(SUM(s.quantity_on_hand), 0) * 100.0) / w.capacity, 2) AS utilization_pct FROM warehouses w LEFT JOIN stock_items s ON w.warehouse_id = s.warehouse_id GROUP BY w.warehouse_id, w.name, w.capacity ORDER BY utilization_pct DESC, w.warehouse_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Left joins facilities with inventory and computes ratio against nominal capacity.
hints: Use `ROUND((COALESCE(SUM(s.quantity_on_hand), 0) * 100.0) / w.capacity, 2)`.
Group by `w.warehouse_id, w.name, w.capacity`.

Query: SELECT w.warehouse_id, w.name, w.capacity, COALESCE(SUM(s.quantity_on_hand), 0) AS total_units_stored, ROUND((COALESCE(SUM(s.quantity_on_hand), 0) * 100.0) / w.capacity, 2) AS utilization_pct FROM warehouses w LEFT JOIN stock_items s ON w.warehouse_id = s.warehouse_id GROUP BY w.warehouse_id, w.name, w.capacity ORDER BY utilization_pct DESC, w.warehouse_id ASC;

title: Calculate Average Item Cost and SKU Breadth by Supplier
description_markdown: Procurement pricing review: For each supplier providing inventory items, count supplied items (`COUNT(s.item_id)` as `item_count`) and compute the average unit cost (`ROUND(AVG(s.unit_cost), 2)` as `avg_unit_cost`). Return `sp.name AS supplier_name`, `item_count`, and `avg_unit_cost`. Order by `avg_unit_cost` DESC, `sp.supplier_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT sp.name AS supplier_name, COUNT(s.item_id) AS item_count, ROUND(AVG(s.unit_cost), 2) AS avg_unit_cost FROM suppliers sp JOIN stock_items s ON sp.supplier_id = s.supplier_id GROUP BY sp.supplier_id, sp.name ORDER BY avg_unit_cost DESC, sp.supplier_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Aggregates pricing benchmarks per vendor.
hints: Join `suppliers sp` and `stock_items s` on `sp.supplier_id = s.supplier_id`.
Group by `sp.supplier_id, sp.name` and order by `avg_unit_cost` DESC, `sp.supplier_id` ASC.

Query: SELECT sp.name AS supplier_name, COUNT(s.item_id) AS item_count, ROUND(AVG(s.unit_cost), 2) AS avg_unit_cost FROM suppliers sp JOIN stock_items s ON sp.supplier_id = s.supplier_id GROUP BY sp.supplier_id, sp.name ORDER BY avg_unit_cost DESC, sp.supplier_id ASC;

title: Identify Most Expensive SKU per Warehouse Facility
description_markdown: Using a window ranking function, find the single product with the highest `unit_cost` stored in each warehouse. If tied, pick the lowest `item_id`. Return `warehouse_id`, `sku`, `name`, and `unit_cost`. Order by `warehouse_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: WITH RankedItems AS (SELECT warehouse_id, sku, name, unit_cost, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY warehouse_id ORDER BY unit_cost DESC, item_id ASC) AS rn FROM stock_items) SELECT warehouse_id, sku, name, unit_cost FROM RankedItems WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY warehouse_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Uses ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by warehouse and filtered to rank 1.
hints: Use `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY warehouse_id ORDER BY unit_cost DESC, item_id ASC)` in a CTE.
Filter outer query with `WHERE rn = 1`.

Query: WITH RankedItems AS (SELECT warehouse_id, sku, name, unit_cost, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY warehouse_id ORDER BY unit_cost DESC, item_id ASC) AS rn FROM stock_items) SELECT warehouse_id, sku, name, unit_cost FROM RankedItems WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY warehouse_id ASC;

title: Retrieve Latest Movement Log per Active Item
description_markdown: Logistics tracking: Find the most recent transaction entry for each item that has activity in `stock_transactions`. Return `item_id`, `tx_id`, `transaction_type`, `quantity`, and `tx_date`. Order by `item_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: WITH LatestTx AS (SELECT item_id, tx_id, transaction_type, quantity, tx_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY item_id ORDER BY tx_date DESC, tx_id DESC) AS rn FROM stock_transactions) SELECT item_id, tx_id, transaction_type, quantity, tx_date FROM LatestTx WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY item_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Applies ROW_NUMBER() ordered by transaction timestamp descending.
hints: Use `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY item_id ORDER BY tx_date DESC, tx_id DESC)`.
Filter in outer query where `rn = 1`.

Query: WITH LatestTx AS (SELECT item_id, tx_id, transaction_type, quantity, tx_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY item_id ORDER BY tx_date DESC, tx_id DESC) AS rn FROM stock_transactions) SELECT item_id, tx_id, transaction_type, quantity, tx_date FROM LatestTx WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY item_id ASC;

title: Calculate Safety Stock Coverage Ratio
description_markdown: Inventory risk analysis: Calculate the stock coverage ratio for every product: `ROUND((quantity_on_hand * 1.0) / reorder_level, 2)` as `coverage_ratio`. Return `sku`, `name`, `quantity_on_hand`, `reorder_level`, and `coverage_ratio`. Order by `coverage_ratio` ASC, `sku` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT sku, name, quantity_on_hand, reorder_level, ROUND((quantity_on_hand * 1.0) / reorder_level, 2) AS coverage_ratio FROM stock_items ORDER BY coverage_ratio ASC, sku ASC;
solution_explanation: Evaluates current stock against reorder threshold ratios.
hints: Divide `(quantity_on_hand * 1.0)` by `reorder_level` and round to 2 decimals.
Order by `coverage_ratio` ASC, `sku` ASC.
Query: SELECT sku, name, quantity_on_hand, reorder_level, ROUND((quantity_on_hand * 1.0) / reorder_level, 2) AS coverage_ratio FROM stock_items ORDER BY coverage_ratio ASC, sku ASC;

title: Dense Rank Products by Total On-Hand Asset Value
description_markdown: Rank products across the catalog by total holding valuation (`quantity_on_hand * unit_cost` as `total_val`) using `DENSE_RANK()` as `value_rank`. Return `sku`, `name`, `total_val`, and `value_rank`. Order by `value_rank` ASC, `sku` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT sku, name, (quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) AS total_val, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY (quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) DESC) AS value_rank FROM stock_items ORDER BY value_rank ASC, sku ASC;
solution_explanation: Applies DENSE_RANK window function ordered by asset value descending.
hints: Use `DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY (quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) DESC)`.
Order by `value_rank` ASC, `sku` ASC.
Query: SELECT sku, name, (quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) AS total_val, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY (quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) DESC) AS value_rank FROM stock_items ORDER BY value_rank ASC, sku ASC;

title: Aggregate Outbound Fulfillment Dispatch Units by Hub
description_markdown: Calculate total units dispatched via outbound transactions for each warehouse facility (`COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.transaction_type = 'outbound' THEN t.quantity ELSE 0 END), 0)` as `total_outbound`). Include warehouses with zero outbound activity. Return `w.warehouse_id`, `w.name`, and `total_outbound`. Order by `total_outbound` DESC, `w.warehouse_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT w.warehouse_id, w.name, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.transaction_type = 'outbound' THEN t.quantity ELSE 0 END), 0) AS total_outbound FROM warehouses w LEFT JOIN stock_items s ON w.warehouse_id = s.warehouse_id LEFT JOIN stock_transactions t ON s.item_id = t.item_id GROUP BY w.warehouse_id, w.name ORDER BY total_outbound DESC, w.warehouse_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Joins warehouses through stock items to movement logs with conditional sum.
hints: Use `LEFT JOIN` twice from warehouses to stock_items to stock_transactions.
Sum with `CASE WHEN t.transaction_type = 'outbound' THEN t.quantity ELSE 0 END`.

Query: SELECT w.warehouse_id, w.name, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.transaction_type = 'outbound' THEN t.quantity ELSE 0 END), 0) AS total_outbound FROM warehouses w LEFT JOIN stock_items s ON w.warehouse_id = s.warehouse_id LEFT JOIN stock_transactions t ON s.item_id = t.item_id GROUP BY w.warehouse_id, w.name ORDER BY total_outbound DESC, w.warehouse_id ASC;

title: Calculate Cumulative Transaction Flow per Item
description_markdown: For all records in `stock_transactions`, calculate the cumulative running total of units moved per item: `SUM(quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY item_id ORDER BY tx_date ASC, tx_id ASC)` as `running_qty`. Return `tx_id`, `item_id`, `transaction_type`, `quantity`, `tx_date`, and `running_qty`. Order by `item_id` ASC, `tx_date` ASC, `tx_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT tx_id, item_id, transaction_type, quantity, tx_date, SUM(quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY item_id ORDER BY tx_date ASC, tx_id ASC) AS running_qty FROM stock_transactions ORDER BY item_id ASC, tx_date ASC, tx_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Computes a running sum partition over chronological item events.
hints: Use `SUM(quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY item_id ORDER BY tx_date ASC, tx_id ASC)`.
Order by `item_id` ASC, `tx_date` ASC, `tx_id` ASC.

Query: SELECT tx_id, item_id, transaction_type, quantity, tx_date, SUM(quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY item_id ORDER BY tx_date ASC, tx_id ASC) AS running_qty FROM stock_transactions ORDER BY item_id ASC, tx_date ASC, tx_id ASC;

title: Compare Item Unit Cost Against Catalog Maximum
description_markdown: Using an empty window frame `MAX(unit_cost) OVER ()`, calculate the cost difference between the most expensive item in the catalog and each product: `(MAX(unit_cost) OVER () - unit_cost)` as `diff_from_max`. Return `sku`, `name`, `unit_cost`, and `diff_from_max`. Order by `diff_from_max` ASC, `sku` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT sku, name, unit_cost, (MAX(unit_cost) OVER () - unit_cost) AS diff_from_max FROM stock_items ORDER BY diff_from_max ASC, sku ASC;
solution_explanation: Compares individual item costs to the global catalog maximum.
hints: Use `MAX(unit_cost) OVER () - unit_cost` as `diff_from_max`.
Order by `diff_from_max` ASC, `sku` ASC.
Query: SELECT sku, name, unit_cost, (MAX(unit_cost) OVER () - unit_cost) AS diff_from_max FROM stock_items ORDER BY diff_from_max ASC, sku ASC;

title: Calculate Replenishment Deficit and Procurement Costs
description_markdown: Procurement action report: For products that have fallen strictly below their reorder threshold (`quantity_on_hand < reorder_level`), calculate the unit deficit (`(reorder_level - quantity_on_hand)` as `stock_deficit`) and the direct capital required to restore inventory to the reorder level (`(reorder_level - quantity_on_hand) * unit_cost` as `replenishment_cost`). Return `sku`, `name`, `quantity_on_hand`, `reorder_level`, `stock_deficit`, and `replenishment_cost`. Order by `replenishment_cost` DESC, `sku` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT sku, name, quantity_on_hand, reorder_level, (reorder_level - quantity_on_hand) AS stock_deficit, ((reorder_level - quantity_on_hand) * unit_cost) AS replenishment_cost FROM stock_items WHERE quantity_on_hand < reorder_level ORDER BY replenishment_cost DESC, sku ASC;
solution_explanation: Computes shortage quantity and procurement cost to restore baseline inventory.
hints: Filter with `WHERE quantity_on_hand < reorder_level`.
Compute `(reorder_level - quantity_on_hand) * unit_cost` as `replenishment_cost`.

Query: SELECT sku, name, quantity_on_hand, reorder_level, (reorder_level - quantity_on_hand) AS stock_deficit, ((reorder_level - quantity_on_hand) * unit_cost) AS replenishment_cost FROM stock_items WHERE quantity_on_hand < reorder_level ORDER BY replenishment_cost DESC, sku ASC;

title: Map Supplier Sourcing Density Across Warehouse Facilities
description_markdown: Supply chain network matrix: For each active warehouse and supplier relationship present in `stock_items`, count the number of catalog items provided (`COUNT(s.item_id)` as `item_count`). Return `w.name AS warehouse_name`, `sp.name AS supplier_name`, and `item_count`. Order by `item_count` DESC, `w.warehouse_id` ASC, `sp.supplier_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT w.name AS warehouse_name, sp.name AS supplier_name, COUNT(s.item_id) AS item_count FROM stock_items s JOIN warehouses w ON s.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id JOIN suppliers sp ON s.supplier_id = sp.supplier_id GROUP BY w.warehouse_id, w.name, sp.supplier_id, sp.name ORDER BY item_count DESC, w.warehouse_id ASC, sp.supplier_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Aggregates multi-table inventory cross relationships.
hints: Join `stock_items s` with `warehouses w` and `suppliers sp`.
Group by warehouse and supplier primary keys and names.

Query: SELECT w.name AS warehouse_name, sp.name AS supplier_name, COUNT(s.item_id) AS item_count FROM stock_items s JOIN warehouses w ON s.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id JOIN suppliers sp ON s.supplier_id = sp.supplier_id GROUP BY w.warehouse_id, w.name, sp.supplier_id, sp.name ORDER BY item_count DESC, w.warehouse_id ASC, sp.supplier_id ASC;

title: Calculate Line-Item Share of Warehouse Asset Value
description_markdown: Asset concentration analysis: For each SKU in `stock_items`, calculate what percentage of its warehouse facility's total inventory value it represents: `ROUND(((quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) * 100.0) / SUM(quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) OVER (PARTITION BY warehouse_id), 2)` as `pct_of_warehouse_val`. Return `warehouse_id`, `sku`, `name`, and `pct_of_warehouse_val`. Order by `warehouse_id` ASC, `pct_of_warehouse_val` DESC, `sku` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT warehouse_id, sku, name, ROUND(((quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) * 100.0) / SUM(quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) OVER (PARTITION BY warehouse_id), 2) AS pct_of_warehouse_val FROM stock_items ORDER BY warehouse_id ASC, pct_of_warehouse_val DESC, sku ASC;
solution_explanation: Computes percentage contribution within each warehouse partition.
hints: Use window aggregate `SUM(quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) OVER (PARTITION BY warehouse_id)`.
Multiply line item value by 100.0 before dividing and rounding.

Query: SELECT warehouse_id, sku, name, ROUND(((quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) * 100.0) / SUM(quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) OVER (PARTITION BY warehouse_id), 2) AS pct_of_warehouse_val FROM stock_items ORDER BY warehouse_id ASC, pct_of_warehouse_val DESC, sku ASC;

title: Calculate Inventory Outbound Turnover Velocity
description_markdown: Calculate outbound inventory velocity: for each product in `stock_items`, calculate total units dispatched via outbound transactions (`COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.transaction_type = 'outbound' THEN t.quantity ELSE 0 END), 0)` as `total_dispatched`) and the ratio of dispatched units to current on-hand stock (`ROUND((total_dispatched * 1.0) / s.quantity_on_hand, 2)` as `turnover_ratio`). Return `s.sku`, `s.name`, `s.quantity_on_hand`, `total_dispatched`, and `turnover_ratio`. Order by `turnover_ratio` DESC, `s.sku` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT s.sku, s.name, s.quantity_on_hand, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.transaction_type = 'outbound' THEN t.quantity ELSE 0 END), 0) AS total_dispatched, ROUND((COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.transaction_type = 'outbound' THEN t.quantity ELSE 0 END), 0) * 1.0) / s.quantity_on_hand, 2) AS turnover_ratio FROM stock_items s LEFT JOIN stock_transactions t ON s.item_id = t.item_id GROUP BY s.item_id, s.sku, s.name, s.quantity_on_hand ORDER BY turnover_ratio DESC, s.sku ASC;
solution_explanation: Measures turnover speed by contrasting cumulative outbound shipments with remaining inventory.
hints: Use `LEFT JOIN stock_transactions t ON s.item_id = t.item_id`.
Group by product fields and compute turnover ratio.

Query: SELECT s.sku, s.name, s.quantity_on_hand, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.transaction_type = 'outbound' THEN t.quantity ELSE 0 END), 0) AS total_dispatched, ROUND((COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN t.transaction_type = 'outbound' THEN t.quantity ELSE 0 END), 0) * 1.0) / s.quantity_on_hand, 2) AS turnover_ratio FROM stock_items s LEFT JOIN stock_transactions t ON s.item_id = t.item_id GROUP BY s.item_id, s.sku, s.name, s.quantity_on_hand ORDER BY turnover_ratio DESC, s.sku ASC;

title: Track Previous Transaction Timestamp with Window LAG
description_markdown: Audit transaction intervals: For each movement in `stock_transactions`, retrieve the timestamp of the immediate preceding transaction for the same item using `LAG(tx_date) OVER (PARTITION BY item_id ORDER BY tx_date ASC, tx_id ASC)` as `prev_tx_date`. Return `tx_id`, `item_id`, `transaction_type`, `quantity`, `tx_date`, and `prev_tx_date`. Order by `item_id` ASC, `tx_date` ASC, `tx_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT tx_id, item_id, transaction_type, quantity, tx_date, LAG(tx_date) OVER (PARTITION BY item_id ORDER BY tx_date ASC, tx_id ASC) AS prev_tx_date FROM stock_transactions ORDER BY item_id ASC, tx_date ASC, tx_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Applies LAG window offset to retrieve preceding movement event dates.
hints: Use `LAG(tx_date) OVER (PARTITION BY item_id ORDER BY tx_date ASC, tx_id ASC)`.
Order by `item_id` ASC, `tx_date` ASC, `tx_id` ASC.

Query: SELECT tx_id, item_id, transaction_type, quantity, tx_date, LAG(tx_date) OVER (PARTITION BY item_id ORDER BY tx_date ASC, tx_id ASC) AS prev_tx_date FROM stock_transactions ORDER BY item_id ASC, tx_date ASC, tx_id ASC;

title: Detect Suppliers Dominating Global Inventory Value
description_markdown: Supplier concentration risk: Find suppliers whose provided items represent at least 15% of the company's total catalog inventory valuation (`val_share_pct >= 15.0`). Return `sp.supplier_id`, `sp.name`, `SUM(s.quantity_on_hand * s.unit_cost)` as `supplier_val`, and `ROUND((SUM(s.quantity_on_hand * s.unit_cost) * 100.0) / (SELECT SUM(quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) FROM stock_items), 2)` as `val_share_pct`. Order by `val_share_pct` DESC, `sp.supplier_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT sp.supplier_id, sp.name, SUM(s.quantity_on_hand * s.unit_cost) AS supplier_val, ROUND((SUM(s.quantity_on_hand * s.unit_cost) * 100.0) / (SELECT SUM(quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) FROM stock_items), 2) AS val_share_pct FROM suppliers sp JOIN stock_items s ON sp.supplier_id = s.supplier_id GROUP BY sp.supplier_id, sp.name HAVING ROUND((SUM(s.quantity_on_hand * s.unit_cost) * 100.0) / (SELECT SUM(quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) FROM stock_items), 2) >= 15.0 ORDER BY val_share_pct DESC, sp.supplier_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Aggregates inventory value per supplier and compares to global subquery valuation.
hints: Use scalar subquery `(SELECT SUM(quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) FROM stock_items)` as denominator.
Filter in HAVING clause with `>= 15.0`.

Query: SELECT sp.supplier_id, sp.name, SUM(s.quantity_on_hand * s.unit_cost) AS supplier_val, ROUND((SUM(s.quantity_on_hand * s.unit_cost) * 100.0) / (SELECT SUM(quantity_on_hand * unit_cost) FROM stock_items), 2) AS val_share_pct FROM suppliers sp JOIN stock_items s ON sp.supplier_id = s.supplier_id GROUP BY sp.supplier_id, sp.name HAVING val_share_pct >= 15.0 ORDER BY val_share_pct DESC, sp.supplier_id ASC;
